getLawyer.why: If arrested or detained in Costa Rica, ask to contact your embassy and a lawyer, and for an interpreter. Pre-trial detention can be long; say nothing and sign nothing without counsel.
Drug possession and trafficking carry severe penalties — lengthy jail or heavy fines. Contact your embassy and a local lawyer immediately.

deadlines.title: Tourist stay — up to 180 days (officer sets it)
deadlines.rule: Tourists may stay up to 180 DAYS; the immigration officer sets your allowed length at entry. Overstaying can lead to deportation and a 5–10 YEAR bar on re-entry. Get and keep your entry stamp.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Costa Rica

deadlines.title: Driving — carry your passport; fines paid at bank
deadlines.rule: A valid foreign licence works up to 180 days (or your entry-stamp length). When driving you must carry your actual PASSPORT (copies aren't accepted). Fines are NOT paid on the spot — pay at COSEVI or a bank. After an accident, stay and call 911; you may be stopped from leaving the country until injury claims are settled.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Costa Rica

sentencing.name: Drug possession / trafficking (Costa Rica)
sentencing.first_offender: Severe penalties including lengthy jail or heavy fines; a local lawyer is essential.

statutes.title: Carry proof of legal stay; passport when driving
statutes.summary: Carry proof of legal status; when driving you must carry the actual passport (photocopies are not accepted). Authorities may ask for ID at any time, including on public transport.

statutes.title: Right to consular access when detained
statutes.summary: A detained foreign national may have their consulate notified and communicate with it — ask for this immediately if arrested.

book.title: Police, ID, and if you're detained in Costa Rica
book.overview: Costa Rica is a civil-law country and generally safer, but take the usual care. Carry proof of legal stay (and your passport when driving). Fines aren't paid roadside — if an officer asks for money you can decline and complain to the Tourism Bureau. If detained, contact your embassy and a lawyer. Emergency: 911.
your_rights: Carry proof of legal status; the actual passport when driving.
Fines are not payable on the spot — pay at a bank/COSEVI.
If an officer asks you for money, you can refuse and report it to the Costa Rican Tourism Bureau.
If arrested, you have the right to a lawyer, an interpreter, and to contact your embassy.
Do not sign anything without a lawyer and translation.
key_steps: Carry proof of stay; passport when driving; keep a passport copy separately.
If asked for money, decline and say you'll pay any fine at the bank.
If detained: ask for your embassy and a lawyer; say little.
Save 911 and the Embassy of Canada line (+506 2242-4400).
Avoid photographing official buildings (illegal) and demonstrations (foreigners barred from political activity).
common_mistakes: Only carrying a photocopy while driving.
Not contacting the embassy early when detained.
book.when_lawyer: If detained, arrested, or in any drug matter: contact your embassy and a local lawyer immediately.

book.title: Entry, tourist stay, and overstaying in Costa Rica
book.overview: Tourists may stay up to 180 days (the officer decides the actual number). Get an entry stamp and keep a copy. Overstaying can bring deportation and a long re-entry bar.
your_rights: Visa-free tourist stays up to 180 days (officer sets the number).
You're entitled to your entry stamp — verify the days granted.
You must keep proof of legal stay to exit.
key_steps: Get the entry stamp and photograph it.
Check the days granted and don't overstay.
Carry proof of onward travel and funds if asked.
For longer stays or residency, get local immigration advice.
book.when_lawyer: For overstays or residency, consult a Costa Rican immigration lawyer; your embassy can refer one.

book.title: Arrested or charged in Costa Rica
book.overview: The system is civil-law and pre-trial detention can be long; drug penalties are severe. Contact your embassy, get a local lawyer and interpreter, and say nothing without them.
your_rights: Right to a lawyer, an interpreter, and to contact your embassy.
Presumption of innocence, but pre-trial detention can be long.
key_steps: Ask immediately to contact your embassy and a lawyer.
Do not sign or admit anything without counsel and translation.
Have someone notify family and the embassy's 24/7 line.
common_mistakes: Talking to police without a lawyer/interpreter.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately — a local criminal lawyer with embassy help; treat drugs as an emergency.

sources.title: Government of Canada — Costa Rica travel advice

book.statute: Costa Rica Penal Code; Code of Criminal Procedure

book.title: Emergencies and staying safe in Costa Rica
book.overview: Dial 911 for any emergency. Petty theft is the main risk — watch valuables, use registered transport, and don't leave belongings unattended on beaches. Keep your embassy's number handy.
your_rights: Call 911 for police, fire, or ambulance.
Your embassy has a 24/7 line for citizens in distress.
You can report crimes and get a report for insurance.
key_steps: After a crime, report it (OIJ) and get a written report.
Use hotel safes and registered transport; don't leave items unattended.
In danger, call 911 first, then your embassy.
common_mistakes: Leaving valuables on the beach or in cars.
book.when_lawyer: For injury, a serious crime against you, or detention, contact your embassy for local lawyer referrals.
